questions.label: 19-20 1(b)
questions.text: What is aperture of an Antenna? Show how antenna aperture can be set to increase directivity of an antenna.
questions.points: Effective aperture $A_e = P_r/S$: the area that collects the received power. $D = 4\pi A_e/\lambda^2 = 4\pi\varepsilon_{ap}A_p/\lambda^2$, so an aperture large in wavelengths and uniformly lit gives a high directivity and a narrow beam.
draws: Diagram: bigger aperture, narrower beam

questions.label: 19-20 1(d)
questions.text: Calculate the half power beamwidth, beamwidth between first nulls, radiated power and directivity of an antenna with power pattern $sin\theta sin\varphi$ for $0 \le \theta \le \pi,~0 \le \varphi \le \pi$.
questions.method: Find where $U = U_m/2$ and $U = 0$ in the principal planes; $P_{rad} = \iint U\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi$; $D = 4\pi U_m/P_{rad}$.
draws: Graph: the pattern in its two principal planes

questions.label: 18-19 1(b)
questions.text: Calculate the half power beamwidth, beamwidth between first nulls, radiated power and directivity of an antenna with power pattern $\cos^2\theta\sin\varphi$ for $0 \le \theta \le \pi$, $0 \le \varphi \le \pi$.
questions.method: Find where $U = U_m/2$ (HPBW) and $U = 0$ (FNBW) in the principal plane; $P_{rad} = \iint U\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi$ over the given ranges; $D = 4\pi U_m/P_{rad}$.
draws: Graph: the pattern in two cuts

questions.label: 19-20 5(d)
questions.text: Define near field and far field for an antenna.
questions.points: Reactive near field out to $0.62\sqrt{D^3/\lambda}$ ($1/r^2$, $1/r^3$ terms, stored energy); radiating near (Fresnel) field out to $2D^2/\lambda$ (pattern still depends on $r$); far (Fraunhofer) field beyond, only $1/r$ terms, fixed pattern, $E/H = \eta$.

questions.label: 18-19 1(d)
questions.text: For an elemental magnetic dipole derive the equation for electric field and magnetic field intensity.
questions.outline: Vector potential of a small current loop; $H = \nabla\times A/\mu$ in spherical coordinates; $E$ from $\nabla\times H = j\omega\varepsilon E$; collect the terms in $1/r$, $1/r^2$, $1/r^3$; far field keeps $1/r$.
draws: Diagram: small current loop and the field point

questions.label: 19-20 1(c)
questions.text: Describe how passive remote sensing is used to detect object.
questions.points: A radiometer's antenna collects the thermal noise objects emit, $T_B = eT_{phys}$; averaged over the beam it gives $T_A$ and power $P = kT_AB$; an object shows as a contrast in $T_B$ against its background (metal looks cold); resolution $\Delta T = T_{sys}/\sqrt{B\tau}$.
draws: Diagram: passive remote sensing with a radiometer
compare: Passive vs active remote sensing: measures natural thermal emission vs sends a signal and measures the echo (radar)

questions.label: 19-20 4(c)
questions.text: Explain how the RADAR range equation is used to detect object.
questions.points: Echo power $P_r = P_tG^2\lambda^2\sigma/((4\pi)^3R^4)$; detection needs $P_r \ge P_{min}$, so $R_{max} = [P_tG^2\lambda^2\sigma/((4\pi)^3P_{min})]^{1/4}$; range from the echo delay, $R = ct/2$.
draws: Diagram: radar geometry, outgoing wave and echo

questions.label: 18-19 2(c)
questions.text: Show the signal to noise ratio of a radio link is related to bandwidth and system temperature.
questions.outline: Power density $P_tG_t/(4\pi r^2)$; received power with $A_e = G_r\lambda^2/4\pi$; noise power $kT_{sys}B$; divide: $S/N = P_tG_tG_r\lambda^2/((4\pi r)^2kT_{sys}B)$.
draws: Diagram: radio link with signal and noise at the receiver

questions.label: 18-19 6(c)
questions.text: Show that for antennas with same aperture the received to transmitted power ratio is inversely proportional to square of wavelength and distance between them.
questions.outline: Isotropic density $P_t/(4\pi r^2)$; directive antenna multiplies by $D = 4\pi A/\lambda^2$; received power = density × $A$; ratio $P_r/P_t = A^2/(r^2\lambda^2)$ (Friis for equal apertures).

questions.label: 19-20 5(c)
questions.text: Derive the equation for a uniform linear array and write the conditions for main beam direction, width of main beam and null locations.
questions.outline: Phase step $\psi = \beta d\cos\theta + \delta$; add $N$ elements: geometric series; sum it; write with sines; normalize: $|AF_n| = |\sin(N\psi/2)/(N\sin(\psi/2))|$; main beam at $\psi = 0$, nulls at $\psi = \pm2k\pi/N$.
draws: Diagram: array geometry and array factor

questions.label: 18-19 3(a)i
questions.text: Write short notes on. (i) Lorentz reciprocity theorem.
questions.points: Lorentz reciprocity: $\int E_2\cdot J_1\,dV = \int E_1\cdot J_2\,dV$ for linear, isotropic media; so an antenna has the same pattern and impedance transmitting and receiving.

questions.label: 18-19 3(a)ii
questions.text: Write short notes on. (ii) Image theory.
questions.points: Image theory: a perfect conductor plane can be replaced by the mirror image of the sources (horizontal current reversed, vertical current kept) without changing the fields above it.
draws: Diagram: sources above a conductor and their images

questions.label: 18-19 3(b)
questions.text: Write the steps to determine line input impedance using Smith Chart.
questions.points: Normalize $z_L = Z_L/Z_0$ and plot it; draw the SWR circle through it; rotate clockwise (towards the generator) by $l/\lambda$ on the wavelength scale; read $z_{in}$; multiply by $Z_0$.

questions.label: 20-21 1(c)
questions.text: In Fig. 1, a lossless transmission line is shown where, $V(z) = V_0^+(e^{-j\beta z} + \Gamma e^{j\beta z})$, $I(z) = \frac{V_0^+}{Z_0}(e^{-j\beta z} - \Gamma e^{j\beta z})$, $\Gamma$ is the reflection coefficient at point $z = 0$, $Z_0$ is the characteristics impdedance of the line, $Z_L$ is the load impedance, and $\beta$ is the phase constant. Show that (i) $\Gamma = \frac{Z_L - Z_0}{Z_L + Z_0}$ (ii) $Z_{in}(l) = \left(\frac{Z_L - jZ_0\tan\beta l}{Z_0 - jZ_L\tan\beta l}\right)Z_0$
questions.outline: $Z(z) = V/I$ from the given waves; at $z = 0$, $Z = Z_L$: solve for $\Gamma$; put $\Gamma$ in at $z = l$; group terms; Euler; divide by $2\cos\beta l$.
draws: Diagram: line with load and $Z_{in}$ (Fig. 1)
Graph: standing-wave patterns

questions.label: 19-20 6(c)
questions.text: Briefly describe input impedance for open circuit termination and short circuit termination.
questions.points: $Z_{sc} = jZ_0\tan\beta l$, $Z_{oc} = -jZ_0\cot\beta l$: pure reactances; below $\lambda/4$ a short looks inductive, an open capacitive; they swap every $\lambda/4$ and repeat every $\lambda/2$; lossy: $Z_0\tanh\gamma l$, $Z_0\coth\gamma l$; $Z_0 = \sqrt{Z_{oc}Z_{sc}}$.
draws: Graph: input reactance of short- and open-circuited lines
compare: Short-circuited vs open-circuited line: $jZ_0\tan\beta l$, inductive below $\lambda/4$ vs $-jZ_0\cot\beta l$, capacitive below $\lambda/4$

questions.label: 18-19 3(c)
questions.text: A lossless transmission line length $0.434\lambda$ and characteristic impedance $100~\Omega$ is terminated in an impedance $260 + j180~\Omega$. Find the voltage reflection coefficient, standing wave ratio and the location of maximum voltage on the line.
questions.method: $\Gamma_L = (Z_L - Z_0)/(Z_L + Z_0)$; SWR $= (1 + |\Gamma|)/(1 - |\Gamma|)$; first voltage maximum where the phase of $\Gamma(d) = \Gamma_Le^{-j2\beta d}$ is 0: $d = \theta_\Gamma\lambda/(4\pi)$.
questions.answer: $\Gamma_L = 0.598\angle21.8°$; SWR = 3.98; first maximum $0.0303\lambda$ from the load
draws: Diagram: the load on a Smith chart

questions.label: 18-19 4(c)
questions.text: Derive the equation for a short circuit terminated transmission line and sketch voltage, current and impedance as a function of line length.
questions.outline: General solution $V_0^+(e^{-j\beta z} + \Gamma e^{j\beta z})$; a short gives $\Gamma = -1$; voltage $-2jV_0^+\sin\beta z$, current $(2V_0^+/Z_0)\cos\beta z$; ratio a distance $l$ from the short: $Z_{in} = jZ_0\tan\beta l$.
draws: Graph: voltage, current and reactance along a short-circuited line

questions.label: 19-20 6(a)
questions.subtopic: RF behaviour of L and C
questions.text: Explain how radio frequency affects the inductor and capacitor reactance.
questions.points: $X_L = \omega L$ grows and $X_C = 1/\omega C$ falls with frequency, so parasitics matter: a capacitor's lead inductance makes it series-resonant at $1/2\pi\sqrt{L_sC}$ and inductive above; an inductor's winding capacitance makes it parallel-resonant and capacitive above (self-resonant frequency).
draws: Circuit: real L and C models at RF

questions.label: 18-19 4(a)
questions.subtopic: RF behaviour of L and C
questions.text: Sketch the equivalent circuit of a high frequency resistor. Also plot a typical frequency versus impedance cure  *[sic: should be curve]* of the resistor.
questions.points: $R$ with the parasitic capacitance $C_a$ in parallel and the lead inductance $L$ in series; $|Z|$ is $R$ at low frequency, falls above $f = 1/(2\pi RC_a)$, has a series-resonance minimum, then rises with the lead reactance.
draws: Circuit: high-frequency resistor model
Graph: impedance of a resistor against frequency

questions.label: 20-21 6(a)
questions.text: What are the uses of a microstrip line? Mention its advantages. Describe the type of losses in a microstrip line.
questions.points: Uses: RF and microwave PCB interconnects, printed filters, couplers, dividers, matching networks, patch antennas, MICs and MMICs. Advantages: small, light, cheap, planar, easy to mount devices, $Z_0$ set by the strip width. Losses: conductor (skin effect), dielectric, radiation, surface waves.
draws: Diagram: microstrip cross-section and field

questions.label: 18-19 4(b)
questions.text: What is microstrip antenna? Mention some of the applications of microstrip line.
questions.points: Microstrip antenna: a metal patch about half a wavelength long over a ground plane on a dielectric substrate, radiating from its open edges; low profile, cheap, narrow band. Microstrip lines: MIC and PCB interconnects, matching networks, filters, couplers, array feeds.
draws: Diagram: microstrip patch fed by a line

questions.label: 20-21 2(c)

questions.points: A $\lambda/4$ section of impedance $Z_1$ turns a load $R_L$ into $Z_{in} = Z_1^2/R_L$; with $Z_1 = \sqrt{Z_0R_L}$, $Z_{in} = Z_0$. Limits: real loads only (or move to a real point first), exact at one frequency (narrow band), $Z_1$ must be realizable.

questions.text: For high pass filter determine ABCD parameters of a two port system.
questions.outline: ABCD of a series impedance $[1, Z; 0, 1]$ and of a shunt admittance $[1, 0; Y, 1]$; cascade by matrix product; put in $Z = 1/(j\omega C)$ and $Y = 1/(j\omega L)$.

questions.label: 18-19 5(b)
questions.text: What are stability circles? Explain how it is used.
questions.points: Stability circles: the loci on the $\Gamma_L$ (or $\Gamma_S$) plane where $|\Gamma_{in}| = 1$ (or $|\Gamma_{out}| = 1$); one side is stable; choose source and load only in the stable region; unconditional stability when no circle cuts the chart ($K > 1$, $|\Delta| < 1$).
draws: Diagram: output stability circle on the $\Gamma_L$ plane

questions.label: 18-19 5(c)
questions.text: Explain the working principle of negative resistance oscillator and feedback oscillator.
questions.points: Negative-resistance oscillator: a device with $R_{in} < 0$ and a resonant load, oscillating when $R_{in} + R_L = 0$ and $X_{in} + X_L = 0$. Feedback oscillator: an amplifier with a frequency-selective feedback network, oscillating when $|A\beta| = 1$ and the loop phase is zero (Barkhausen).
draws: Block diagram: negative-resistance and feedback oscillators
compare: Negative-resistance vs feedback oscillator: one-port device with $R_{in} < 0$ vs amplifier with a feedback loop, $|A\beta| = 1$

questions.label: 18-19 5(d)
questions.text: A lossless transmission line of length 1.5 m, which is less than quarter wavelength has open circuit impedance $-j54.6~\Omega$ and short circuit impedance $j103~\Omega$. Find $Z_o$ and $\gamma$. Also find the input impedance if the line length is doubled and the length of line if it is to appear as an open circuit at the input.
questions.method: $Z_0 = \sqrt{Z_{oc}Z_{sc}}$; $\tan\beta l = \sqrt{Z_{sc}/Z_{oc}}$ (imaginary parts); for the doubled length use $Z_{sc} = jZ_0\tan2\beta l$, $Z_{oc} = -jZ_0\cot2\beta l$.

questions.label: 18-19 6(a)i
questions.text: Write short notes on the following topics. (i) Poincare Sphere
questions.points: Poincaré sphere: each polarization is one point; linear polarizations on the equator, circular at the poles (left and right), elliptical in between; latitude sets the ellipticity, longitude the tilt.
draws: Diagram: the Poincaré sphere

questions.label: 18-19 6(a)ii
questions.text: Write short notes on the following topics. (ii) Yagi-Uda antenna.
questions.points: Yagi-Uda: an end-fire array of one driven half-wave dipole, a slightly longer reflector behind it and several shorter directors in front, coupled parasitically; high gain in one direction; TV and VHF/UHF links.
draws: Diagram: Yagi-Uda antenna

questions.label: 18-19 6(b)
questions.text: For a paraboloid-of-revolution with an isotropic point source what is the ratio of power density and field intensity ratio.
questions.outline: Parabola $r = 2f/(1 + \cos\theta)$; radius on the aperture $\rho = r\sin\theta$; power in a cone maps to an annulus; ratio to the centre $S(\theta)/S(0) = [(1 + \cos\theta)/2]^2$; field ratio its square root.
draws: Diagram: paraboloid with the source at the focus

questions.label: 18-19 6(d)
questions.text: For a pyramidal or rectangular horn show that directivity D is $D \approx 10\log(\frac{7.5A_p}{\lambda^2})$.
questions.outline: $D = 4\pi A_e/\lambda^2$; $A_e = \varepsilon_{ap}A_p$; a horn has $\varepsilon_{ap} \approx 0.6$; $4\pi \times 0.6 \approx 7.5$; in dB $10\log(7.5A_p/\lambda^2)$.
draws: Diagram: pyramidal horn

questions.label: 19-20 1(a)
questions.text: Write short notes on the following topics (i) Directivity (ii) Effective Height (iii) Beam Area
questions.points: Directivity $D = U_{max}/U_{av} = 4\pi U_{max}/P_{rad} = 4\pi/\Omega_A$ (isotropic 1, half-wave dipole 1.64). Effective height $h_e = V_{oc}/E$: the length of an equivalent antenna with uniform current equal to the terminal current ($\lambda/\pi$ for a half-wave dipole). Beam area $\Omega_A = \iint P_n(\theta, \phi)\,d\Omega$: the solid angle through which all the power would flow at the peak intensity; $D = 4\pi/\Omega_A$; $\Omega_A \approx \theta_{HP}\phi_{HP}$.
draws: Diagram: real pattern and its equivalent beam-area cone
Diagram: effective height of a half-wave dipole

questions.label: 20-21 2(a)
questions.text: Derive the equation of the constant resistance and constant reactance circle of a Smith Chart. You should start form the relation between the reflection coefficient and the normalized load.
questions.outline: Write $z = (1 + \Gamma)/(1 - \Gamma)$ with $\Gamma = u + jv$; rationalize and split real and imaginary parts; complete the square: $r$-circles centre $(r/(1 + r), 0)$, radius $1/(1 + r)$; $x$-circles centre $(1, 1/x)$, radius $1/|x|$.
draws: Diagram: $z$ plane mapped into the unit circle
Diagram: constant-r circles and constant-x arcs

questions.outline: Write $z = (1 + \Gamma)/(1 - \Gamma)$ with $\Gamma = u + jv$; rationalize and split real and imaginary parts; complete the square: $r$-circles centre $(r/(1 + r), 0)$, radius $1/(1 + r)$; $x$-circles centre $(1, 1/x)$, radius $1/|x|$.

Diagram: constant-r circles and constant-x arcs

questions.label: 19-20 2(b)
questions.text: Write the properties of r-circles and x-circles of a Smith chart.
questions.points: r-circles: centres on the real axis, all through $(1, 0)$, shrinking from the unit circle ($r = 0$) to the point $(1, 0)$ ($r = \infty$); $r = 1$ through the centre. x-circles: centres on $u = 1$, radius $1/|x|$, all through $(1, 0)$; $+x$ above, $-x$ below; the real axis is $x = 0$; the two families cross at right angles.
draws: Diagram: the landmarks of the Smith chart
compare: r-circles vs x-circles: centres on the real axis, inside the chart vs centres on $u = 1$, arcs above and below the axis

questions.label: 19-20 2(c)
questions.text: Describe how TE mode is different from TM mode in a circular waveguide.
questions.points: TE: $E_z = 0$, cutoff from zeros of $J_n'$, dominant TE$_{11}$ ($p'_{11} = 1.841$), $Z_{TE} > \eta$. TM: $H_z = 0$, cutoff from zeros of $J_n$, lowest TM$_{01}$ ($p_{01} = 2.405$), $Z_{TM} < \eta$.
draws: Diagram: TE11 and TM01 fields in a circular guide
compare: TE vs TM modes: $E_z = 0$, cutoff from zeros of $J_n'$, $Z > \eta$ vs $H_z = 0$, cutoff from zeros of $J_n$, $Z < \eta$

questions.label: 19-20 2(d)
questions.text: The input impedance of a short-circuited lossy transmission line of length 2 m and characteristics impedance 75 $\Omega$ is $15 + j120~\Omega$. Find $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of the line. Determine the input impedance if the sort-circuit  *[sic: should be short-circuit]* is replaced by a load impedance $Z_L = 37 + j45~\Omega$.
questions.method: $Z_{in} = Z_0\tanh\gamma l$ for a short: solve $\tanh\gamma l = Z_{in}/Z_0$ for $\gamma l$ (inverse tanh); $\alpha$ and $\beta$ from its parts; then the general formula with the new load.

questions.label: 19-20 3(a)
questions.text: Why we use S-parameters for microwave analysis? Define S-matrix for 3 port network with appropriate example.
questions.points: At microwave frequencies opens and shorts are hard to make and can make devices oscillate, while matched loads and wave power are easy to measure (VNA); so networks are described by $b = [S]a$, $S_{ij} = b_i/a_j$ with the other ports matched. Three-port example: a power divider or circulator.
draws: Diagram: three-port network with incident and outgoing waves
compare: S-parameters vs Z/Y parameters: waves with matched ports, measurable at microwave vs voltages and currents with open or short ports

questions.label: 19-20 3(b)
questions.text: Explain the condition for constant gain for amplifier.
questions.points: Unilateral amplifier ($S_{12} \approx 0$): $G_{TU} = G_SG_0G_L$; $G_S$ is constant when $\Gamma_S$ lies on a circle with centre $d_{gs} = g_sS_{11}^*/[1 - |S_{11}|^2(1 - g_s)]$ and radius $r_{gs} = \sqrt{1 - g_s}(1 - |S_{11}|^2)/[1 - |S_{11}|^2(1 - g_s)]$; same for $G_L$.
draws: Block diagram: unilateral amplifier with input and output matching networks

questions.label: 19-20 3(c)
questions.text: For the figure shown in Fig. 1 draw the flow graph and derive the input impedance formula at port 1 from the signal flow-graph representation.
questions.outline: One equation per branch; draw the flow graph; $\Gamma_{in}$ = path from $a_1$ to $b_1$: $\Gamma_Le^{-j2\beta l}$; $Z_{in} = Z_0(1 + \Gamma_{in})/(1 - \Gamma_{in})$; put in $\Gamma_L$, Euler, divide by $2\cos\beta l$.
draws: Diagram: signal flow graph of the loaded line

questions.label: 19-20 3(d)
questions.text: A FET is operated at $f = 4$ GHz and is biased such that $s_{11} = 0.7\angle 125^\circ$. It is assumed that the transistor is unconditionally stable. Find the maximum source gain $G_{Smax}$ and sketch the constant gain circles for several values of $G_S$.
questions.outline: $G_{Smax} = 1/(1 - |S_{11}|^2)$ at $\Gamma_S = S_{11}^*$; for each chosen $G_S$ the normalized $g_s = G_S/G_{Smax}$; circle centre $d_{gs}$ and radius $r_{gs}$; draw them on the line at the angle of $S_{11}^*$.
draws: Diagram: constant source-gain circles on the Smith chart

questions.label: 19-20 4(a)i
questions.text: Write short notes on the following topic (i) Reflection coefficient
questions.points: $\Gamma = V^-/V^+ = (Z_L - Z_0)/(Z_L + Z_0)$; $|\Gamma| \le 1$ for a passive load; along the line $\Gamma(d) = \Gamma_Le^{-j2\beta d}$; 0 when matched, $-1$ short, $+1$ open.

questions.label: 19-20 4(a)ii
questions.text: Write short notes on the following topic (ii) Standing wave ratio
questions.points: $S = |V|_{max}/|V|_{min} = (1 + |\Gamma|)/(1 - |\Gamma|)$, $1 \le S < \infty$; maxima and minima are $\lambda/4$ apart; $S = 1$ matched, infinite for a short or open.
draws: Graph: standing-wave patterns for three loads

questions.label: 19-20 4(a)iii
questions.text: Write short notes on the following topic (iii) RF radiation hazards and safety standard
questions.points: RF fields heat tissue (eyes and testes most sensitive); limits set by ICNIRP/IEEE as SAR (W/kg) or power density, stricter for the public than for workers and varying with frequency; keep distance, shield, limit exposure time.
draws: Graph: ICNIRP reference levels for power density

questions.label: 20-21 6(c)
questions.text: A rectangular cavity resonator has dimensions of $a = 5$ cm, $b = 2$ cm, and $d = 15$ cm. Compute the resonant frequency of the dominant mode for a dielectric-field cavity of $\epsilon_r = 2.56$.
questions.method: $u' = c/\sqrt{\varepsilon_r}$; dominant mode TE$_{101}$ since $d > a > b$; $f_r = (u'/2)\sqrt{(1/a)^2 + (1/d)^2}$.
draws: Diagram: cavity and its dominant mode

questions.label: 19-20 4(a)iv
questions.text: Write short notes on the following topic (iv) Microwave cavity resonators
questions.points: A closed metal box (or section of guide shorted at both ends) resonates when its length is a whole number of half guide-wavelengths; $f_{mnl} = \frac{c}{2\pi\sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r}}\sqrt{(m\pi/a)^2 + (n\pi/b)^2 + (l\pi/d)^2}$; very high Q; used in filters, oscillators and wavemeters.
draws: Diagram: rectangular cavity and its TE101 field

questions.label: 19-20 5(a)
questions.text: Derive the equations for wave impedance, cut-off frequency, and phase constant for a transverse magnetic wave.
questions.outline: Maxwell's curl equations give the transverse fields from $E_z$; wave equation for $E_z$; separate variables; walls force $\sin(m\pi x/a)\sin(n\pi y/b)$; $\beta = \sqrt{k^2 - k_c^2}$; cutoff at $\beta = 0$; transverse fields; $Z_{TM} = \eta\beta/k$.
draws: Diagram: rectangular guide
Graph: TM $\beta$ and impedance against frequency

questions.label: 19-20 5(b)
questions.text: Find the forward voltage gain of a high-pass filter.
questions.outline: Voltage division $R/(R + 1/j\omega C)$; write as $j(f/f_c)/(1 + jf/f_c)$; magnitude and phase; $G_V = 20\log|H|$.
draws: Circuit: RC high-pass filter
Graph: its gain

questions.label: 20-21 1(a)
questions.text: From the lumped-element equivalent circuit, derive the expression of the propagation constant in terms of series resistance $R$, series inductance $L$, shunt conductance $G$, and shunt capacitance $C$ per unit length. Deduce this expression to low-loss transmission line.
questions.outline: KVL and KCL on a section $\Delta z$; divide by $\Delta z$, let it go to 0: telegrapher's equations; phasors; wave equation $V'' = \gamma^2V$ with $\gamma = \sqrt{(R + j\omega L)(G + j\omega C)}$; low loss: drop $RG$, $\sqrt{1 + x} \approx 1 + x/2$.
draws: Circuit: lumped-element model of a short line
Waveform: travelling wave without and with loss

questions.label: 19-20 6(b)
questions.text: From the general equation of transmission line find the expressions for characteristic impedance and reflection coefficient.
questions.outline: $I = -(1/(R + j\omega L))\,dV/dz$; differentiate $V_0^\pm e^{\mp\gamma z}$; $Z_0 = (R + j\omega L)/\gamma = \sqrt{(R + j\omega L)/(G + j\omega C)}$; at the load $V/I = Z_L$; solve for $\Gamma_L = V_0^-/V_0^+$.
draws: Circuit: lumped model of a short piece of line
Diagram: line with the load at $z = 0$

questions.label: 19-20 6(d)
questions.text: The standing wave ratio on a lossless 50 $\Omega$ transmission line terminated in an unknown load impedance is found to be 2. The distance between the successive voltage minima is 15 cm, and the first minimum is located at 5 cm from the load. Determine reflection coefficient, load impedance and equivalent length and terminating resistance of a line such that the input impedance is equal to $Z_L$.
questions.method: $\lambda = 2 \times$ minima spacing; $|\Gamma| = (S - 1)/(S + 1)$; phase from the first minimum, $\theta_\Gamma = 2\beta d_{min} - \pi$; $Z_L = Z_0(1 + \Gamma)/(1 - \Gamma)$.
draws: Graph: measured standing wave and the equivalent line

questions.label: 20-21 1(b)
questions.text: If the propagation constant of a transmission line is $50\angle 89.38^\circ~\text{m}^{-1}$, $R = 4~\Omega~\text{m}^{-1}$, $L = 0.5~\mu\text{H}~\text{m}^{-1}$, $C = 200~\text{pF}~\text{m}^{-1}$, calculate the value of shunt conductance with proper unit.
questions.method: $\gamma$ into $\alpha$, $\beta$; $\omega$ from $\beta = \omega\sqrt{LC}$; $Z_0 = \sqrt{L/C}$; $\alpha_c = R/2Z_0$; $G = 2(\alpha - \alpha_c)/Z_0$; check $R \ll \omega L$, $G \ll \omega C$.

questions.label: 20-21 3(b)
questions.text: A telephone line has $R = 30~\Omega~\text{km}^{-1}$, $L = 100~\text{mH}~\text{km}^{-1}$, $G = 0$, and $C = 20~\mu\text{F}~\text{km}^{-1}$. At $f = 1$ kHz, obtain: (i) The characteristic impedance of the line (ii) The propagation constant (iii) The phase velocity
questions.method: $Z_0 = \sqrt{(R + j\omega L)/(G + j\omega C)}$; $\gamma = \sqrt{(R + j\omega L)(G + j\omega C)}$; $u_p = \omega/\beta$.

questions.label: 20-21 3(a)
questions.text: A plane wave in a nonmagnetic medium has $\vec{E} = 50\sin(10^8t + 2z)\hat{a}_y$ V/m. Find: (i) The direction of wave propagation (ii) $\lambda$, $f$, and $\epsilon_r$ (iii) $\vec{H}$
questions.method: Read $\omega$ and $\beta$ from the argument $\omega t + \beta z$ (+ sign: travels in $-z$); $\lambda = 2\pi/\beta$, $f = \omega/2\pi$; $\varepsilon_r = (\beta c/\omega)^2$; $\eta = 120\pi/\sqrt{\varepsilon_r}$; $\vec H$ with $\vec E \times \vec H$ along the propagation.
questions.answer: $-\hat a_z$; $\lambda = 3.142$ m, $f = 15.92$ MHz, $\varepsilon_r = 36$; $\vec H = 0.796\sin(10^8t + 2z)\hat a_x$ A/m
draws: Diagram: the plane wave with $E$, $H$ and propagation

questions.label: 20-21 3(d)
questions.text: A rectangular waveguide with dimensions $a = 2.5$ cm, $b = 1$ cm is to operate below 15.1 GHz. How many TE and TM modes can the waveguide transmit if the guide is filled with a medium characterized by $\sigma = 0$, $\epsilon = 4\epsilon_0$, $\mu_r = 1$? Calculate the cutoff frequencies of the modes.
questions.method: $u' = 1/\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}$; $f_c = (u'/2)\sqrt{(m/a)^2 + (n/b)^2}$; list TE ($m$ or $n$ may be 0) and TM ($m, n \ge 1$) modes below 15.1 GHz.
questions.answer: 11 TE and 4 TM modes; TE$_{10}$ at 3 GHz
draws: Diagram: TE10 field across the guide
Graph: cutoff frequencies of the filled guide

questions.label: 20-21 4(a)
questions.text: The magnetic vector potential of a Hertzian dipole is given by: $\vec{A} = \frac{\mu_0 Idl}{4\pi r}e^{-j\beta r}\hat{z}$. Show that magnetic field, $H = \frac{Idl}{4\pi}\cos(\theta)\left[\frac{j\beta}{r} + \frac{1}{r^2}\right]e^{-j\beta r}\hat{\phi}$  *[sic: should be $\sin(\theta)$]*.
questions.outline: Write $\mathbf{A}$ in spherical components; curl in spherical coordinates (only the $\phi$ part survives); the two derivatives; combine; divide by $\mu_0$.
draws: Diagram: Hertzian dipole and spherical coordinates

questions.label: 20-21 4(b)
questions.text: Using the expression of $H$ found in 4(a), show that the electric field component $E = \frac{\eta Idl}{4\pi}\cos(\theta)\left[\frac{j\beta}{r} + \frac{1}{r^2} - \frac{j}{\beta r^3}\right]e^{-j\beta r}\hat{\theta} + \frac{\eta Idl}{2\pi}\cos(\theta)\left[\frac{1}{r^2} - \frac{j}{\beta r^3}\right]e^{-j\beta r}\hat{r}$  *[sic: the $\hat{\theta}$ term should have $\sin(\theta)$]*
questions.outline: $\mathbf{E} = (1/j\omega\varepsilon)\nabla\times\mathbf{H}$ with only $H_\phi$; radial part from $\partial(\sin\theta H_\phi)/\partial\theta$; polar part from $\partial(rH_\phi)/\partial r$; write with $\eta$ and $\beta$.
draws: Graph: how the $1/r$, $1/r^2$ and $1/r^3$ terms compare with distance

questions.label: 20-21 4(c)
questions.text: Find the expression of average power density of Hertzian dipole in far field zone.
questions.outline: Far field keeps the $1/r$ terms: $E_\theta = \eta H_\phi$; $\mathbf{P}_{avg} = \tfrac12\text{Re}(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{H}^*)$; put in $|H_\phi|$; free space $\eta = 120\pi$.
draws: Graph: radiation pattern of a Hertzian dipole

questions.label: 20-21 5(a)
questions.text: An RF signal at $f = 100$ MHz is mixed with local oscillator signal at $f_{LO} = 90$ MHz. (i) Calculate the IF (intermediate frequency) output. (ii) Why are active filters used after mixing in a super-heterodyne receiver?
questions.method: $f_{IF} = f_{RF} - f_{LO}$; the sum and the image ($f_{LO} - f_{IF}$) are rejected by filters.
questions.answer: $f_{IF} = 10$ MHz; filters pick the IF and reject the sum, leakage and adjacent channels
draws: Block diagram: superheterodyne receiver
Spectrum: frequencies around the mixer

questions.label: 20-21 5(b)
questions.text: For a 1 kHz message signal modulating a 1 MHz carrier with 80% modulation index in AM, calculate the total transmitted power if carrier power is 100 W.
draws: Waveform: AM wave and its power spectrum

questions.label: 20-21 5(c)
questions.text: For an antenna with gain 10 dB transmitting 10 W power at 2.4 GHz, calculate the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) of the antenna.
draws: Diagram: directive antenna and its isotropic equivalent

questions.label: 20-21 5(d)i
questions.text: Write short notes (any three). (i) Klystron
questions.points: Klystron: electrons velocity-modulated in the buncher cavity bunch in the drift space and give energy to the catcher cavity; high-gain, narrow-band amplifier (reflex klystron as an oscillator).
draws: Diagram: two-cavity klystron
Graph: Applegate diagram

questions.label: 20-21 5(d)ii
questions.text: Write short notes (any three). (ii) Magnetron
questions.points: Magnetron: crossed dc E and B fields make electrons rotate as spokes that excite a ring of resonant cavities; efficient high-power oscillator (radar, microwave ovens).
draws: Diagram: cavity magnetron cross-section

questions.label: 20-21 5(d)iii
questions.text: Write short notes (any three). (iii) Gunn Diode Oscillator
questions.points: Gunn diode: in n-GaAs above a threshold field electrons move to a heavier valley, giving negative differential mobility; travelling domains make current pulses at a frequency set by the length; low-power microwave source.
draws: Graph: Gunn effect velocity-field curve

questions.label: 20-21 5(d)iv
questions.text: Write short notes (any three). (iv) Travelling Wave Tube (TWT)
questions.points: TWT: an electron beam travels along a helix slow-wave structure at nearly the wave's speed, giving energy to the wave continuously; very wide-band, high-gain amplifier (satellite transponders).
draws: Diagram: helix travelling-wave tube
compare: Klystron vs TWT: resonant cavities, narrow band vs helix slow-wave line, very wide band

questions.label: 20-21 6(b)
questions.text: Derive Jefeminko's equation and from there, explain the necessity of accelerating charge for electromagnetic radiation.
questions.outline: Retarded potentials; $\nabla t_r = -\hat R/c$ and $\nabla(1/R) = -\hat R/R^2$; gradient of $V$ and time derivative of $\mathbf{A}$ give $\mathbf{E}$; curl of $\mathbf{A}$ gives $\mathbf{B}$; the $1/R$ terms need $\dot\rho$ and $\dot{\mathbf{J}}$: radiation needs accelerating charges.
draws: Diagram: source point, field point and retarded time
Diagram: why a stopping charge radiates

questions.label: 20-21 6(d)
questions.text: What do you mean by effective height and effective area of an antenna?
questions.points: Effective height $h_e = V_{oc}/E$: the length of an equivalent uniform-current antenna ($\lambda/\pi$ for a half-wave dipole). Effective area $A_e = P_{received}/S_{incident} = G\lambda^2/4\pi$: the area that collects the received power.
draws: Diagram: effective height of a half-wave dipole
compare: Effective height vs effective area: open-circuit voltage per field (m) vs received power per power density (m$^2$)
